Q. Q. 4 اِزْبَأَرَّ It (fur, or soft hair, and a plant, or herbage) grew forth. (S, K, TA.) ―
-b2- It (hair) bristled up. (S, A, K.) ―
-b3- He (a dog [and a horse]) bristled up his hair. (S, K.) Marrár Ibn-Munkid El-Handhalee says, (S, TA,) describing a horse, (TA,) “فَهْوَ وَرْدُ اللَّوْنِ فِى ٱزْبِئْرَارِهِ
وَكُمَيْتُ اللَّوْنِ مَا لَمْ يَزْبَئِرْ
” [And he is of a yellowish red colour on the occasion of his bristling up his hair, and of a dark bay colour as long as he does not bristle up his hair]. (S, TA.) ―
-b4- Also He (a cat) had abundance of hair. (TA.) ―
-b5- And He (a man) prepared for evil, or mischief: (K, TA:) or became affected by a quaking, or trembling, and a bristling-up of the hair. (TA)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
